## Legacy $x_1$ wall routines: isentropic wall ghosts and the wall-face state copy (no switch) {#sec-ch05-legacy}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: OUTLINE.md 5.10; src/hydro/hydro.cpp; src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp (described from the code)

### Summary

Two routines treat a stratified column at a wall without the well-balanced reconstruction: one fills the ghost cells
with an isentropic continuation of the wall cell, the other makes the two states at the wall face agree. The ghost fill's call in `HydroImpl::forward` is commented out; the face copy runs only on the $x_1$ path
taken when `wb_x1` is false and gravity is on, a combination no configuration reaches with a pressure row.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Two wall treatments of the non-well-balanced $x_1$ path: an isentropic extrapolation of $p$ and $\rho$
into the wall ghosts (defined, never called) and a copy of the right state's $p$ and $\rho$ into the left state at
the wall face (@eq-ch05-legacy-copy).

**Data.** In and out: the wall ghosts, or the left and right states at the wall face.

**Placement.** The copy would run after the $x_1$ reconstruction, at physical $x_1$ walls; the ghost fill's call is
commented out.

**Activation.** None. Effectively unreachable: with gravity on and any EOS other than `shallow-water` the
well-balanced path of @sec-ch05-wbx1 runs instead, and the shallow-water EOS has no pressure row for these routines.

**Guarantee / limits.** N/A: not maintained.

**Evidence.** No test exercises either routine.
:::

### Derivation

The face copy sets, at the lower wall face $i_s-\tfrac12$ (and symmetrically at the upper one),

$$
\begin{aligned}
p^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow p^{R}_{i_s-1/2}, \\
\rho^{L}_{i_s-1/2} &\leftarrow \rho^{R}_{i_s-1/2},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-legacy-copy}

in `_revise_x1inner_lr`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_lr >}}),
so the Riemann solver sees no pressure jump at the wall. The ghost fill holds $K=p/\rho^\gamma$ of the wall cell and
integrates $\mathrm{d}(p^{a})/\mathrm{d}x_1=-a\,g/K^{1/\gamma}$, $a=(\gamma-1)/\gamma$, cell by cell into the ghosts, the
isentropic hydrostatic profile, in `_revise_x1inner_ghost`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_revise_x1inner_ghost >}}).
Neither is used at the pin, so neither has a check.

### Numerical method

The copy is shown in @fig-ch05-legacy-lr. It would run after the $x_1$ reconstruction, in every stage, on the faces of
physical $x_1$ walls.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-legacy-lr
#| fig-cap: "The legacy wall-face copy at a bottom wall (thick black line), $x_1$ to the right: the left state's $p$ and $\\rho$ at the wall face (orange triangle on the ghost side) are overwritten by the right state's (bluish-green arrow). The vermillion line under the hatched ghost cells marks the isentropic ghost fill, whose call is commented out."
#| fig-alt: "Two hatched ghost cells and three interior cells meeting at a wall; two triangles at the wall face with an arrow from the right one to the left one; a line under the ghost cells."
```

### Tests

No test exercises either routine at the pin; the live call is unreachable in every registered test.

### Limits

1. **Dead code.** The ghost fill is never called and the face copy is unreachable with a pressure row; they are kept,
   not maintained.
2. **If revived.** The isentropic fill assumes one $\gamma$ for the column and an isentropic wall region; it would
   conflict with the even-parity perturbation ghosts of @sec-ch05-wbx1.
